card.name: End of a serious condition term
card.fires_on: The last piece of a serious adverse-condition term in warnings, such as shock, hyperthermia or thyrotoxicosis, or the verb right after it. It appears where the sentence is about to say what happened or what is needed.

modes.label: Ending of a condition name
modes.description: Final piece of a medical term for a severe condition such as shock, malignant hyperthermia or thyrotoxicosis.
modes.example: Signs consistent with malignant hyperther<<mia>> may include hyperthermia, hypox

modes.label: Verb after a condition
modes.description: The helping verb right after a list of losses or symptoms, before a past participle.
modes.example: Significant fluid losses from vomiting and diarrhea<< have>> required intravenous fluid administration.

card.plain: It fires at the end of a severe condition name in a warning, just before the text says what followed from it.
